newsitem.title: USA: Ergo says dopamine therapy treats diabetes.
newsitem.headline: Ergo says dopamine therapy treats diabetes.

text.p: Ergo Science Corp said Tuesday that studies on mice show combination therapy with certain drugs known as dopamine D1/D2 agonists significantly improves basic metabolic derangements of Type II diabetes.
Ergo said its researchers found that a combination of dopamine Dl/D2 agonists had good effects on blood levels of insulin, glucose, lipids and free fatty acids.
The combination also had positive effects on proteins, enzymes and other measures related to diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular health, Ergo said.

"With this combination treatment, we can transform the physiology of a mouse that is genetically predisposed to obesity, high blood lipids and blood sugar levels to produce a lean animal with normal blood sugar and lipid levels," said Anthony Cincotta, Ergo's chief scientific officer.
Ergo said it would present the preclinical findings at the Annual Scientific Sessions of the American Diabetes Association June 21-24.
